o: No change in LH or FSH levels
Acting directly as an LH analog
pharm-repro:hpg.e: Loss of negative feedback → ↑ GnRH, LH, FSH; used in PCOS infertility.

pharm-repro:hpg.q: A 24-year-old female marathon runner has had no menses for 8 months. BMI is 17 kg/m², pregnancy test is negative, LH, FSH and estradiol are low, and prolactin and TSH are normal. Mechanism of her amenorrhea?
o: Primary ovarian failure with ↑ FSH feedback
Androgen excess from ovarian theca cells
pharm-repro:hpg.e: Functional hypothalamic amenorrhea (energy deficit, exercise) suppresses GnRH pulses → low LH/FSH/estradiol; ovarian failure would give high FSH.

pharm-repro:gnrh.e: Also central precocious puberty; initial testosterone flare can be blocked with flutamide.

pharm-repro:gnrh.q: Degarelix differs from leuprolide because it:
o: Is a GnRH antagonist with no flare
Is a GnRH agonist with a flare

pharm-repro:gnrh.q: A 72-year-old man with metastatic prostate cancer and vertebral metastases starts leuprolide. One week later he has worsening back pain and urinary retention. Which drug given at initiation would have prevented this?
pharm-repro:gnrh.e: Continuous GnRH agonist first causes an LH and testosterone flare; an androgen receptor blocker (or a GnRH antagonist instead) prevents it. Finasteride does not block testosterone action.

pharm-repro:estrogen.e: Endometrial cancer if unopposed; add progestin if the uterus is present.

o: Prior DVT or ER+ breast cancer

pharm-repro:estrogen.q: A 53-year-old woman with an intact uterus takes estradiol alone for hot flashes. Two years later she has postmenopausal bleeding, and endometrial biopsy shows hyperplasia without atypia. What should have been added to her regimen?
pharm-repro:estrogen.e: Unopposed estrogen drives endometrial proliferation; a progestin protects the endometrium. Tamoxifen is itself an endometrial agonist.

pharm-repro:serm.e: Agonist at bone, antagonist at breast and uterus; ↑ VTE.
Used in ER+ postmenopausal breast cancer and ovulation induction.

pharm-repro:serm.q: A 58-year-old postmenopausal woman has taken a drug for 3 years after resection of an ER-positive breast cancer. She now has vaginal bleeding, and ultrasound shows a thickened endometrium. Her bone density has been preserved. Mechanism of this adverse effect?
o: Estrogen receptor blockade at the endometrium
Partial estrogen agonism at the endometrium
Progesterone receptor agonism in the uterus
pharm-repro:serm.e: Tamoxifen is an antagonist at breast but an agonist at endometrium and bone → endometrial hyperplasia/cancer; aromatase inhibitors would cause bone loss, not endometrial growth.

pharm-repro:progestin.e: Combined with misoprostol for medical abortion.
Loss of bone mineral density; depot contraceptive every 3 months.

pharm-repro:progestin.q: A 26-year-old woman at 7 weeks' gestation by ultrasound requests medical termination of pregnancy. She receives a standard two-drug regimen, the second being misoprostol taken 24–48 hours later. The first drug acts by:
pharm-repro:progestin.e: Mifepristone is a progesterone receptor antagonist that destabilizes the decidua; misoprostol (PGE₁ analog) then induces uterine contractions.

pharm-repro:contra.q: Combined oral contraceptives prevent pregnancy mainly by:
o: Directly killing sperm in the vagina

pharm-repro:contra.e: The local reaction is toxic to sperm and ova; non-hormonal; heavier periods.

pharm-repro:contra.q: A 37-year-old woman who smokes 20 cigarettes daily and has migraine with aura requests reliable contraception. Which method is contraindicated?
pharm-repro:contra.e: Estrogen raises the risk of ischemic stroke and VTE, greatest with smoking ≥ 35 years and migraine with aura; progestin-only and copper methods are acceptable.

pharm-repro:androgen.q: Danazol was used for endometriosis and can cause:
pharm-repro:androgen.e: Synthetic androgen, partial agonist; androgenic effects.

pharm-repro:androgen.q: A 26-year-old competitive bodybuilder has acne, gynecomastia and small, soft testes. Hematocrit is 54%, LH and FSH are suppressed, and semen analysis shows azoospermia. Most likely cause?
pharm-repro:androgen.e: Exogenous androgens suppress LH/FSH → testicular atrophy and azoospermia, raise hematocrit, and aromatize to estrogen (gynecomastia). Klinefelter and primary failure have high LH/FSH.

pharm-repro:antiandrogen.q: Spironolactone is used in PCOS hirsutism because it:
pharm-repro:antiandrogen.e: Also ↓ androgen synthesis; causes gynecomastia in men.
Used with GnRH agonists in prostate cancer.

pharm-repro:antiandrogen.q: A 63-year-old man with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction has taken spironolactone for a year and now has painful bilateral breast enlargement. Mechanism of this adverse effect?
pharm-repro:antiandrogen.e: Spironolactone blocks androgen receptors (and ↓ testosterone synthesis), causing gynecomastia; eplerenone is more selective and avoids it.

o: Induce labor and control postpartum hemorrhage
Stop preterm labor and delay delivery

pharm-repro:labor.e: Delay preterm labor to give steroids.

pharm-repro:labor.q: A 30-year-old woman delivers vaginally after a prolonged labor. Twenty minutes later she has heavy vaginal bleeding; the uterus is soft and boggy above the umbilicus, and the placenta was delivered intact. Most appropriate first drug?
pharm-repro:labor.e: Uterine atony is the commonest cause of postpartum hemorrhage; oxytocin contracts the myometrium. Terbutaline and nifedipine are tocolytics and would relax the uterus.

pharm-repro:uro.q: A 60-year-old man with stable angina takes isosorbide mononitrate daily and asks for a drug for erectile dysfunction. Sildenafil is withheld because both drugs:
pharm-repro:uro.e: Nitrates stimulate guanylyl cyclase (via NO) and PDE5 inhibitors prevent cGMP breakdown; together they cause profound hypotension. Neither acts through cAMP.

title.th: เคสใหญ่: ปัสสาวะกลางคืนบ่อย
title.en: Boss case: Up at night to urinate

boss.case: A 68-year-old man has weak stream, hesitancy and nocturia three times a night. Digital rectal exam: smooth, symmetrically enlarged prostate. PSA mildly elevated for age. He also has erectile dysfunction.

qs.e: Smooth, symmetric enlargement of the transition zone.
Relaxes prostatic and bladder neck smooth muscle.

o: Blocking α₁ receptors in the prostate
qs.e: Shrinks the prostate over months and lowers PSA ~50%.

qs.q: Tadalafil helps both BPH and ED via:
A key adverse effect of tamsulosin to warn about:
qs.e: Mention before cataract surgery; also first-dose orthostatic hypotension.

qs.q: Which drug class worsens urinary retention and should be avoided?
qs.e: First-generation antihistamines and decongestants also worsen retention.
